deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the opening of a draft letter in German. The salutation reads 'Hochverehrter Herr Professor' (Most honoured Professor). Below it is a crossed-out start ('Die Hin...' and a struck word, possibly 'Fassung'). The surviving text says, roughly: '[The] translation of the last sentence of the prize question:'. Then comes the Latin wording of that sentence, left unfinished: 'Itaque postulat Ordo / theoriam motus fluidorum aequationibus Lagrangianis' ('Therefore the Order [the Faculty] requires ... the theory of the motion of fluids [developed] by means of the Lagrangian equations ...'). The sentence breaks off; presumably a participle such as 'superstructam' or 'expositam' followed (that completion is my conjecture). At the bottom is a small crossed-out scribble.

The Latin almost certainly belongs to the prize question of the Göttingen Philosophical Faculty for 1860/61, which Riemann is generally said to have formulated. It asked for a treatment of hydrodynamics in Lagrangian (material) coordinates. The prize went to Hermann Hankel for 'Zur allgemeinen Theorie der Bewegung der Flüssigkeiten' (Göttingen 1861). The page therefore seems to be Riemann drafting a letter to a colleague about the German rendering or exact wording of the question. The neighbouring pages are unrelated: before it, computations with the rational function y = η^3(η^4+7)/(7η^4+1) and the Laplacian in spherical coordinates; after it, a draft text on plumb-line deflections and the Hanoverian arc measurement.
